era: Arcade / Dreamcast / Game Boy Advance / Xbox / PSP / Mobile
summary: Sega's score-attack taxi-driving series; use Dreamcast/Flycast for the first two games' original music, brands, and maps, Windows for Crazy Taxi 3, and original handheld/mobile releases for the spin-offs.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi

emulation.notes: Use VGA/upscaled Dreamcast output for the complete original home version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution Dreamcast emulation with original licensed presentation intact

primary.why: The Dreamcast version adds the console-only Original map and Crazy Box while retaining the original licensed soundtrack and branded destinations; later HD/PSP ports lose music and/or advertising content, while the arcade original only has the arcade map.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or Flycast with VGA/upscaled output; use later HD/mobile versions only for convenience.

secondary.exclusive_content: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars adds ad-hoc multiplayer modes around the Crazy Taxi/Crazy Taxi 2 content.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP multiplayer modes only if you want the added competitive Fare Wars content.
secondary.why: The PSP compilation removes licensed music/advertising, so it is not the main full-play version.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD/PSP versions have music and branding caveats; mobile versions restore the original soundtrack but are mobile-control/preservation routes.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi 2

emulation.notes: Use Flycast for the full Dreamcast version; PPSSPP only for Fare Wars multiplayer.

primary.why: Crazy Taxi 2 is a Dreamcast original with two New York-inspired cities, new drivers, Crazy Hop, and Crazy Pyramid content; the later PSP compilation adds multiplayer but removes the original licensed soundtrack/advertising.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or Flycast with VGA/upscaled output; use Fare Wars only for PSP multiplayer.

secondary.exclusive_content: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars adds ad-hoc multiplayer modes to the Crazy Taxi 2 content.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP multiplayer modes only.
secondary.why: The PSP port compromises music/advertising and handheld performance, so it is secondary content rather than the main run.

entries.remaster_caveats: No standalone modern remaster documented; PSP compilation has licensing and performance caveats.

emulation.notes: Use the PC release if compatible; use Xbox emulation only if PC preservation is impractical.

primary.why: Crazy Taxi 3 was released on Xbox first, then arcade, then Windows; the PC route preserves the three-map package and allows the highest modern output when configured well.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatible PC with modern compatibility fixes as needed; use Xbox or arcade hardware for original platform comparison.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: Catch a Ride

emulation.notes: Use mGBA for clean handheld preservation.

primary.why: Catch a Ride is the Game Boy Advance adaptation of Crazy Taxi, using the GBA-specific Rush engine and hardware-limited sprite/3D approach; it is a distinct handheld version rather than a replacement for Dreamcast.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Game Boy Advance hardware or mGBA; treat it as a handheld adaptation to sample after the Dreamcast original.

entries.remaster_caveats: Uses instrumental/altered music rather than the original licensed soundtrack.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for cleaner output; original PSP hardware is needed for authentic ad-hoc use.

primary.why: Fare Wars is a PSP compilation of Crazy Taxi and Crazy Taxi 2 with added ad-hoc multiplayer modes; it is the only non-Dreamcast route for Crazy Taxi 2, but loses the original soundtracks and advertising.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware or PPSSPP, mainly for its multiplayer modes or portable Crazy Taxi 2 access.

entries.remaster_caveats: Compilation/port with licensing and performance compromises, not a definitive replacement for Dreamcast.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: City Rush

emulation.notes: Use preserved compatible mobile hardware/software only where legally available.

primary.why: City Rush is a free-to-play mobile spin-off built around lane-changing touch controls on iOS and Android; iOS is selected as the primary archival row only to keep exactly one primary platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play only if you already have access to a preserved compatible mobile install; there is no documented console/PC version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile spin-off, not a mainline arcade sequel.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi Tycoon

primary.why: Crazy Taxi Tycoon, originally known as Crazy Taxi Gazillionaire, is a mobile idle/business-management spin-off released for iOS and Android and later delisted with servers offline.
primary.how_to_play: There is no reliable current official route; document via preserved mobile installs only where legally available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted free-to-play mobile spin-off with servers reported offline; not a playable modern route.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: World Tour

primary.platform: PlayStation 5 / Xbox Series X|S / Nintendo Switch 2 / Windows
primary.why: World Tour is announced for 2027, so no released version can be evaluated for fidelity, completeness, or exclusive content yet.
primary.how_to_play: Wait for release and revisit after final platform/version details and post-launch comparisons are available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Future entry; keep as needs-research until release and public version comparisons exist.
